correctness.rationale: For the \(S(2,2)\) ruling curve the projection objective has denominator \(s(t)=1+t^2+t^4\) and numerator of degree at most \(4\), so its derivative numerator has degree at most \(6\). For the displayed rational data projection \(Q\), exact arithmetic gives the degree-\(6\) polynomial \(4t^6+23t^5+32t^4-238t^3-142t-12\) with nonzero discriminant. Its resultants with the pole polynomial and the cut-locus factor are nonzero, and the derivative at infinity is \(4/63\). These are open nonvanishing conditions on the data Grassmannian, so a nonempty Zariski-open set has exactly six valid critical points. The source's scroll theorem independently gives Euclidean distance degree \(6\).

value.rationale: The initiating paper uses rational normal scrolls as its first concrete ED example and makes the ED-versus-GD comparison a central theme. The balanced scroll S(2,2) is the smallest two-row case allowed by that theorem and has an unusually low ED degree because the two denominator polynomials coincide. Determining whether the further restriction to Grassmannian data causes another degree drop is therefore a natural first missing comparison. The answer is exact: no additional drop occurs, furnishing a small benchmark for future scroll GD formulas.
